sample_unit: clinical text evaluations across four German datasets
models_evaluated: six open-weight LLM judges (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Whether LLM judges can substitute for expert panel in clinical text evaluation
links.effect: Substituting LLM judge for experts shifted 57.2% of pointwise categories, swapped 41.7% of pairwise winners, missed 10.2% of clinical errors, and inverted clinical priorities.
links.quote: Substituting LLM-as-a-judge for the expert panel shifted 57.2% of pointwise categories, swapped 41.7% of pairwise winners, missed 10.2% of clinical errors, and inverted clinical priorities by overrating the criteria succinct and accurate.

unlisted_practices: Decision-impact analysis to set deployment thresholds for LLM-as-a-judge in clinical evaluation
Testing LLM judges for position and identity bias

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the safety and reliability of using LLM-as-a-judge as an automated quality-control/evaluation practice compared to expert panels for clinical text generation.

primary.practice: automated evaluation using LLM-as-a-judge versus expert human review
